goal: Pinned, reproducible benign corpora that both the atom frequency model (P4.03) and the benchmark harness (P6.15) read, so atom selection and every throughput claim are measured on the same data.
scope: bench/corpus/*.json manifests listing SHA-256, size and source for each file: B1 benign filesystem slice, B2 large benign files, S1 mail streams
bench/fetch.ts or a zav subcommand that downloads or assembles each corpus from public sources (OS package mirrors, language package caches, public document and HTML sets) and verifies every hash
A deterministic sampling rule so a smaller CI subset is a stable prefix of the full corpus
Documentation of sources and licences for every corpus in bench/corpus/README.md
out_of_scope: The malware corpus M1 and adversarial corpus A1 (P5.17, P6.21), which are never fetched by default
The 4-gram model itself (P4.03) and the harness (P6.15)
notes: Manifests only: samples are never committed to the repository
Prefer sources with stable URLs and permissive licences so CI can rebuild the corpus
accept: Fetching B1 and B2 on a clean machine reproduces every listed hash
The CI subset fetches in under 5 minutes
P4.03 and P6.15 both read the same manifests

goal: ts-heic rejects malformed and polyglot inputs before decoding and lets callers run a malware scan first, matching what ts-images gains in P8.19.
scope: Validate the ISOBMFF box structure (sizes, nesting, item locations within the file) before decodeHeic starts work
Detect and report trailing data after the last box, and data hidden between boxes
An optional `scan` hook in the decode options that receives the raw bytes and can refuse the input
Tests with crafted HEIC plus ZIP and HEIC plus HTML polyglots
notes: Use the same option name and result shape P8.19 defines for ts-images so callers wire one hook everywhere
accept: Polyglot fixtures are reported before decode

goal: ts-avif rejects malformed and polyglot inputs before decoding and lets callers run a malware scan first, matching ts-images (P8.19).
scope: Validate the ISOBMFF box structure and item extents before decode
Detect trailing and interleaved data outside declared boxes
An optional `scan` hook in the decode options with the P8.19 result shape
Tests with crafted AVIF polyglots
accept: Polyglot fixtures are reported before decode

goal: ts-videos checks container structure before demuxing untrusted sources and offers the same optional scan hook, so media pipelines get one consistent guard.
scope: Container sanity checks for MP4/MOV (box sizes and extents) and WebM/Matroska (element sizes) before demuxing
Trailing-data detection for file and buffer sources
An optional `scan` hook on createSource for buffer and file sources; URL sources scan after download and before demux
Tests with truncated, oversized-box and polyglot fixtures
out_of_scope: Streaming sources that never complete (documented as unscanned)
accept: Fixtures are rejected or reported as designed

goal: The AI package's image inputs can no longer be used to make the server fetch arbitrary URLs or read arbitrary files. Found while mapping scan hooks (P8.11); it is a separate security fix.
scope: URL inputs: allow only http and https, resolve the host and refuse loopback, link-local, private and metadata ranges (re-checked after every redirect), cap redirects and response size, and require an image content type
File inputs: resolve the path and require it to sit inside a configured allowed root (default: the app's storage directory)
Config for an allowlist of hosts and roots; secure defaults
Tests for each refusal and for normal remote and local images
notes: Describe the fix in the changelog without an exploit walkthrough
accept: Requests to private and loopback addresses are refused, including via redirect
Paths outside the allowed root are refused
Framework tests pass and the fix ships in the next release

goal: Large uploads never stall zig-waf workers: @inspectFile answers from a verdict cache or a bounded budget, and finishes long scans asynchronously instead of blocking the request path.
scope: A content-hash keyed verdict cache shared by the Guardian operator (size-bounded, clean verdicts only, invalidated on database version change)
A per-request scan budget; when it runs out the operator answers `unavailable` and policy decides (detection mode logs, blocking mode can refuse)
Background completion of over-budget scans, with the verdict recorded for the next request carrying the same content and reported to Guardian
Metrics: cache hits, budget exhaustions, background scan latency
out_of_scope: The operator registration and in-process link (P9.07, P9.08)
notes: plugin.zig requires operators not to block; unavailable must never be treated as clean
accept: A 1 GB upload completes under the configured budget with an `unavailable` verdict and a later cached verdict
No worker blocks longer than the budget in a soak test
zig-waf CI and evidence stay green
